sentences.text:
The Honourable Smt. Justice K. Sujana
 Criminal Petition No.3960 of 2024
Order:

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioners, who are arrayed as accused Nos.1 to 8, 11 and 12 in FIR, seeking to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.18 of 2024 on the file of Kaleshwaram Police Station, Jayashankar Bhupalpally District, registered for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 420 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act.

entities.text: Kaleshwaram Police Station, Jayashankar Bhupalpally District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
2. Heard Sri P. Lakshma Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S. Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent No.1 - State.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners/accused Nos.1, 2, 3 and 5 were already arrested by the Police, as such, prayed to direct the police to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C, in respect of petitioners/accused Nos.4, 6 to 8, 11 and 12.
4.

In view of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioners/accused Nos.4, 6 to 8, 11 and 12 to appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 26.04.2024 between 11:00 a.m. and 05:00 p.m. and in turn, the Investigating Officer is directed to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. and also the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1 scrupulously.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: However, the petitioners shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer as an when required by furnishing information and the petitioners shall produce all relevant documents/material required for the purpose of the investigation and the Investigating Officer shall consider the same before filing appropriate report before the learned Magistrate concerned.
5. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short 'Cr.P.C.') by the petitioners, who are arrayed as accused Nos.1 to 8, 11 and 12 in FIR, seeking to quash the proceedings against them in Crime No.18 of 2024 on the file of Kaleshwaram Police Station, Jayashankar Bhupalpally District, registered for the alleged offences punishable under Sections 420 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 7 of Essential Commodities Act.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the petitioners/accused Nos.1, 2, 3 and 5 were already arrested by the Police, as such, prayed to direct the police to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C, in respect of petitioners/accused Nos.4, 6 to 8, 11 and 12.
4.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In view of the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioners/accused Nos.4, 6 to 8, 11 and 12 to appear before the Investigating Officer on or before 26.04.2024 between 11:00 a.m. and 05:00 p.m. and in turn, the Investigating Officer is directed to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C. and also the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar 1 scrupulously.
However, the petitioners shall co-operate with the Investigating Officer as an when required by furnishing information and the petitioners shall produce all relevant documents/material required for the purpose of the investigation and the Investigating Officer shall consider the same before filing appropriate report before the learned Magistrate concerned.
5. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall also stand closed.
